fixes.explanation: The LORD's word for Job is integrity. He tells Satan that Job, His servant, still retains his integrity, even though Satan incited Him against Job to ruin him without cause. Job has already lost his flocks, his herds, his servants and his children (Job 1:13-19). Even after all that, the LORD points to his integrity.

A river would be a nice, neat answer, but Satan never mentions one. The text has him say he's come “From roaming through the earth…” and walking back and forth in it. That's the whole earth, not one riverbank.

That's a fair guess, since joy is a good word, but it isn't the one the LORD uses. He says Job still retains his integrity. The LORD says nothing about Job's joy in this verse. Keep your ear out for integrity, because it comes back a few verses later.

Satan says, “…stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones…” Before this, Satan had been given power over everything Job had (Job 1:12), and now he's asking about Job's own body. He says Job “…will surely curse You to Your face.” This part of the story is a heavy one.
The text says something different. When the three friends lift up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. I think that tells us how much he has changed.

They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head. I think they're shaken by what they see in Job. It's a heavy moment, and the friends meet it with real grief.

The text doesn't have them calling out to Job. They could barely recognize him, and they began to weep aloud. Each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head. Their sorrow comes out loud, in tears and torn robes.
That's right. The text says they sat on the ground with Job for seven days and seven nights. That's a full week of sitting there with him. It's a long time to stay put beside a friend who is hurting.

The text doesn't say that. It says they came to sympathize with Job and comfort him, and no one spoke a word to him “…because they saw how intense his suffering was.” Nothing there says anyone is angry. The silence comes from what they see.
